hero.title: Your live production partner in Brazil.

opening.headline: Producing in Brazil, without the friction.
paragraphs: A great live broadcast starts long before broadcast day. We work directly with your team from the initial brief, aligning creative direction, technical planning, and on-the-ground logistics. Everything runs in English, everything happens on the ground in Brazil.

More than streaming, we direct the experience. From the first call to the final master file, you have one point of contact who knows your production inside out. No language friction. No translation losses. No handoffs to strangers on event day.
Live is unforgiving. You can't reshoot. You can't fix it in post. That's why we treat your broadcast the way a director treats a film — with planning, taste, and technical rigor.

blocks.title: Direction that goes beyond the technical.
blocks.text:
Every great broadcast starts with clear direction. Before the event, we dive into the brief to understand your goals, identify the moments that matter most, and plan every entrance, transition, and audience touchpoint.

On event day, the direction is led by the same team that built the plan with you. That continuity means precise decisions in real time, and fidelity to the concept defined from the start — turning a brief into a live experience executed with craft.

blocks.title: Right-sized budgets. No inflated invoices.
blocks.text:
Every event needs its own solution. Our recommendations don't start from a standard package — they start from your objectives, your format, and the experience you want to create.

We propose only what genuinely adds value. When something isn't justified, we say so. When something you didn't ask for could raise the bar, we recommend it. Every decision is driven by efficiency, strategy, and the best return on your investment.

blocks.title: A commitment to craft.
blocks.text:
More than capturing images, we direct the visual narrative of your event. Every frame, camera move, lens choice, lighting setup, and cut is designed to serve the message and hold the audience.

These are the decisions — often invisible — that turn a standard broadcast into a sophisticated experience. One that reflects your brand's quality and holds attention from start to finish.

steps.text: Send us a WhatsApp message with the details of your event. We reply with questions, not a template quote.

steps.title: Tailored proposal
steps.text: Once we understand the event, we build a proposal with what actually makes sense. No filler items to inflate the price.

steps.title: Technical and creative planning
steps.text: Before the day, we align cameras, platforms, coverage, and contingency plans. You know what will happen before it happens.

steps.title: Broadcast and delivery
steps.text: We direct the live. Afterwards, you receive the master recording files to use however you want.

about.title: Meet the director
about.photoAlt: Guido Ferreira, live production director at Pluma
about.bio:
Pluma's live production direction is led by Guido Ferreira.
Audiovisual director with cinematic training and 10 years of delivered projects. Fluent in English and Portuguese, Guido is your single point of contact from the first message to the final delivery — making the creative and technical decisions in image and sound with the individual attention you'd expect from a boutique studio, and speaking your language every step of the way.
about.closer: Pluma combines that authorial direction with the structure of a full production company on the ground in Brazil.

items.q: Do you work with international clients?
items.a: Yes — international agencies, production companies, and brand teams are a core part of what we do. We serve as your in-country partner in Brazil: you brief us in English, we handle direction, coordination, and delivery on the ground. Everything runs in your language, everything happens on ours.

items.q: Where in Brazil do you operate?
items.a: Our base is in Rio de Janeiro. We operate directly in Rio, São Paulo, and travel to other Brazilian capitals for larger productions. For events outside Brazil, we can travel or coordinate with trusted partners in your region.

items.q: How much lead time do you need to book an event?
items.a: Ideally two to four weeks, especially for events with multiple cameras or simultaneous translation. For international productions with more complex logistics — permits, imported equipment, tighter schedules — we recommend starting the conversation four to eight weeks out. Last-minute events are evaluated case by case.

items.q: Do you handle only the broadcast, or the full physical event too?
items.a: Pluma is an audiovisual production company focused on live broadcast and capture. We work with trusted partners for the physical event side: staging, catering, hospitality, RSVP. For international clients producing in Brazil, we can coordinate the full local team on your behalf — one point of contact, one invoice, no chasing multiple vendors.
Yes. Conventions, festivals, and events with continuous programming are part of what we do.

items.q: Do you provide the internet connection?
items.a: Yes. For critical events, we use redundant internet — a primary link plus backup — ensuring maximum stability and continuity of the broadcast, even in unexpected situations.

items.q: Does the client receive the recording afterwards?
items.a: Yes. We deliver the master recording files at the end of the event or within 48 hours, depending on the case.

items.q: Can I repurpose the recording into other content?
items.a: Yes — and it's one of the reasons we deliver the recording in master quality. Many clients use the live capture as raw material for teasers, social cuts, and institutional pieces. Pluma can also handle the post-event edit as an add-on service if needed.

items.q: Do you handle private broadcasts or only public ones?
items.a: Both. We stream to public platforms (YouTube, Instagram, LinkedIn) and to private environments (Vimeo OTT, corporate platforms, gated sites, invitation-only events). For confidential content, we configure the stream with the necessary security layers.

items.q: What happens if the event runs long?
items.a: The proposal covers an estimated duration with a tolerance margin. If the event significantly overruns on the day, an additional hourly rate is agreed in advance. The idea is no surprises — everything is explicit in the proposal before you sign. Our priority is delivering what you need, regardless of the natural shifts along the way.

items.q: Can I book capture only, without live streaming?
items.a: Yes. If you just need a broadcast-quality recording to use later, without a live stream, we handle multi-camera capture and deliver either edited or raw footage — your call. It's a common service for events where transmission isn't needed but the content will become a piece afterwards.

It varies by scope. To speed up the quote, share: location, duration, and type of event; what needs to be streamed and to how many platforms; available infrastructure at the venue; and how many post-live deliverables you need. If you already have a budget in mind, mention it — we can align expectations and propose a structure that fits.

The proposal includes the full technical crew (direction, operators, and assistants scaled to the event, with wireless communication), equipment (cameras, audio, switcher, encoder), lighting, redundant internet, streaming platform setup, and the master recording files at the end of the event. Items that vary by event — staging, teleprompter, simultaneous translation, or travel to other cities — are listed separately in the proposal, so you have full clarity on what you're paying for.

items.q: How does payment work for international clients?
items.a: Standard terms are 50% deposit on project confirmation and 50% before the event date. For recurring clients or larger events, we can negotiate different terms. We accept international wire transfer in USD, EUR, or BRL, and issue invoices from Pluma Agência e Produtora Audiovisual LTDA (CNPJ 31.226.493/0001-06).

items.q: Do you have a portfolio I can see?
items.a: Yes. Since not every broadcast can be shared publicly (client confidentiality or contract restrictions), we present the live streaming portfolio in conversation, tailored to the type of event you're planning. Tell us what you have in mind and we'll show you the most relevant examples.
